com.multicode.doNotUse: Cards or raised chrome — use bg.surface / bg.surface-raised so panels read as elevated.

com.multicode.use: Disabled control labels, empty-state hints.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Body copy — this step is below the AA body-contrast floor by design.

on-accent.$description: Label ink on the accent fill. Flips by mode: white on the deep light-mode green, near-black on the brighter dark-mode green.

hover.$description: Accent hover step: deepens on light, brightens on dark.

soft.$description: Soft accent fill for selected rows.

good-faint.$description: The quietest success fill: a wash for a whole row that has finished while the person was elsewhere.

com.multicode.use: list-row --finished: the row-wide wash under a good-edge ring. One step under good-soft, because a finished row asks for a look, not an answer, and sits beside rows that must stay readable.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Chips, banners, or anything smaller than a row — those take good-soft. Never as a hover or selection fill.

good-edge.$description: Success ring at edge strength: the good tone let down so a 1px ring reads as an edge, not a wire.

com.multicode.use: list-row --finished: the inset ring around a finished row. Full-strength status.good is for marks and ink; on a hairline around a whole row it out-shouts the needs-input gold it is meant to sit under.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Text, icons, dots, or a focus ring — ink stays full strength, and focus is border.focus.

scrim.$description: Modal/dialog backdrop above panel chrome. A plain translucent layer — never add backdrop-filter to a full-viewport scrim.

com.multicode.use: The backdrop layer behind modals, dialogs, and drawers.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Combining with backdrop-filter blur — full-viewport blur re-renders every frame and tanks pointer framerate.

com.multicode.use: Ink of a file-type glyph whose language wears blue; nothing else.

drawer.$description: The one canonical elevation shadow, shared by drawers and overlay panels.

com.multicode.use: Drawer and overlay-panel elevation — the only drop shadow in the system.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Cards, rows, or hover states — structure comes from hairline borders.

popover.$description: Elevation for trigger-anchored surfaces: popovers, menus, tooltips.

com.multicode.use: Popover, ContextMenu, Select listbox, and Tooltip shells.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Cards, rows, or hover states — structure comes from hairline borders.

modal.$description: Elevation for centred modal shells sitting over a scrim.

com.multicode.use: Modal and ConfirmDialog shells only. In dark mode the value leads with an inset top highlight — the lit edge — because a black drop shadow over a scrimmed near-black ground separates nothing; light mode needs no such line.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Anchored surfaces — those use shadow.popover.

control-raised.$description: Resting elevation for a filled control: a 1px lit top edge over a shallow drop.

com.multicode.use: Filled buttons at rest — the primary and destructive variants. The inset highlight is the light source; the drop is what lifts the control off the surface.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Overlays — those take shadow.popover / shadow.modal / shadow.drawer. Also not for ghost or icon buttons: a borderless control has no edge to light.

control-edge.$description: Resting elevation for a bordered neutral control: the quieter half-step below control-raised.

com.multicode.use: Outlined buttons and other bordered neutral controls at rest. Lights the inner top rim on dark, shades the inner bottom on light — both read as lit from above.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Filled controls — those take shadow.control-raised, which is a full step brighter.

control-pressed.$description: The pressed state of any elevated control: the bevel inverts and the drop is gone.

com.multicode.use: Filled and outlined buttons while :active or [data-pressed]. Replaces the resting shadow outright — it is not layered over it.
com.multicode.doNotUse: A resting state, and never on a control that carries no resting elevation.

ui.$description: Default UI face for prose, labels, and chrome. Load Inter with font-feature-settings 'cv11', 'ss01', 'ss03'.

com.multicode.use: All UI text: labels, body, headings, chrome.

mono.$description: Monospace face for identifiers, code, kbd, and terminals. Load with font-feature-settings 'tnum', 'zero'.

com.multicode.use: Identifiers, code, keyboard shortcuts, numeric IDs.

micro.$description: Micro labels: kbd shortcuts in dense chrome.

com.multicode.use: Micro labels only — kbd shortcuts, dense chrome.

compact.$description: Unchanged: 11px is legible at phone viewing distance and is already the floor.

com.multicode.use: Identifiers, meta rows, help and error text.

compact.$description: One step up. This tier carries identifiers and triage summaries on a phone, where 12px sits under the platform floor for supporting copy.

body.$description: Default body, card titles, row labels, buttons.

com.multicode.use: The default text size for body copy, labels, and controls.

compact.$description: One step up, to the iOS/Material body floor. `principles.md` sets 13px as a MINIMUM for primary content, so 15px exceeds the rule rather than breaking it.

platforms.$note: `compact` is the touch-scale ramp: same step NAMES and same step COUNT as the pointer scale, different values. It exists because a 13px body at 30cm on a phone is not the same physical size as a 13px body at 60cm on a monitor, and the two viewing distances do not cancel. Consumers that cannot load tokens.css at all (React Native) read these values and keep the names, so a surface stays portable between the two even though its pixels do not. NOT consumed by build-tokens.mjs — tokens.css is the pointer scale only, and reproduces byte-identically with these annotations present.

com.multicode.use: Section headings inside panels and drawers.

compact.$description: Collapses onto body. A phone screen rarely earns four distinct sizes, and the '3 font sizes per view' ceiling applies here too — weight separates a heading from its body instead.

com.multicode.use: Panel titles (H2) and inspector titles — keep at most 3 sizes per view.

compact.$description: The screen title, which on a phone is the whole page's heading rather than a panel's. The pointer-scale ramp tops out at 16px because a desktop title sits inside a dense composition; a phone title does not.

com.multicode.use: Body copy and meta text.

medium.$description: Medium weight for labels, buttons, and card titles.

com.multicode.use: Button labels, field labels, row titles.

emphasis.$description: Semibold for headings and selected emphasis.

com.multicode.use: Headings and selected-state emphasis where weight must move with color.
Titles and single-line labels.
Body copy and row labels.
Long-form prose in inspectors and docs.

tight.$description: Optical tightening for titles at 14px and up.

com.multicode.use: font.size.heading and font.size.title, which read loose at their default metrics.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Body or meta text — tightening small text costs legibility.

normal.$description: Default tracking: body, labels, and every row title.

com.multicode.use: All UI text that is not a title or a micro label.

wide.$description: Optical opening for mono identifiers and micro labels.

com.multicode.use: font.family.mono identifiers and font.size.micro labels, which jam at their default metrics.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Uppercase-tracked section headings — the system has none.

xs.$description: Inline glyphs next to body/meta copy.

com.multicode.use: Inline glyphs beside meta copy and inside chips.

compact.$description: Touch. One step up from the pointer scale's 13px: beside the compact ramp's 15px body a 13px glyph reads as a smudge rather than as chrome.

com.multicode.use: The default icon size for rows, toolbars, and close glyphs.
Icons paired with button labels and panel-header affordances.
Empty-state glyphs and large overlay close buttons.
Small inner chips nested inside a rounded parent.

control.$description: Cards, rows, buttons, and inputs in panel chrome.

com.multicode.use: The default control radius: buttons, inputs, cards, rows — keep at most 2 radii per view. Sits on the same 7px step as radius.overlay so a control and the popover it opens share one corner.
Popovers, drawers, and floating surfaces.
Modal shells and the largest overlay surfaces.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Operational chrome — larger radii are marketing-only.

pill.$description: Fully-rounded ends. An idiom, not a step of the shape ramp.

com.multicode.use: Badges, status chips, switch tracks and progress rails — anything whose shape says "this is a marker, not a control". Referenced by liveness, wizard-progress and the list-surface pattern, which spelled var(--sem-radius-pill) before this token existed and therefore rendered square.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Buttons, inputs, cards and rows — those take radius.control. A pill-shaped button wears the badge shape, and the two stop being tellable apart. Nor is this a ramp step: it sits outside the 3/7/9 scale on purpose, so a tool reading sem.radius.* as a ramp must exclude it.

fast.$description: Hover, focus, and small state flips.

com.multicode.use: Hover and focus transitions, small state flips.
Popover enters and list reorders.
Drawer and large-surface enter/exit.

pulse.$description: A one-shot attention pulse. Not a transition step.

com.multicode.use: The single play of a change pulse — a count that just moved, a status icon that just flipped. Long enough to be noticed after the eye arrives, where a transition only has to keep up with a pointer already there. Value taken from the shipped .status-icon-pulse, which hard-coded 620ms.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Transitions and state changes — those take fast / normal / deliberate. A 620ms hover is a control that feels broken. Never loop it either: the pulse means "this just changed", and a loop means "this is still happening".

standard.$description: The single easing curve for all UI motion.

com.multicode.use: Every transition and animation — one ease, no exceptions.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Introducing a second easing curve.

3xs.$description: Hairline gap: a glyph from its label, stacked meta lines.

com.multicode.use: Padding, gap, and margin. Every spacing value in a component comes from this scale.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

com.multicode.use: Padding, gap, and margin. Every spacing value in a component comes from this scale.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

3xl.$description: Overlay inset: modal and drawer body padding.

com.multicode.use: Padding, gap, and margin. Every spacing value in a component comes from this scale.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

4xl.$description: Page-level gutter on wide door surfaces.

com.multicode.use: Padding, gap, and margin. Every spacing value in a component comes from this scale.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Control heights or icon sizes — those have their own scales (sem.size.control.*, sem.icon.size.*).

xs.$description: Dense control height: icon buttons and in-row triggers.

com.multicode.use: Height of icon buttons, controls inside a list row, and dense labelled chrome — toolbar and row actions carrying a font.size.meta label.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Ordinary labelled controls, which start at sm. This step is for dense chrome only: a form field, or a button that is the point of its section, is not dense chrome.

compact.$description: Touch. The pointer ramp's 26px is a mouse target; nothing pressable may sit under the hit-target floor, so the whole control ramp lifts by a constant 10px and keeps its shape.

sm.$description: Default control height: buttons, inputs, selects.

com.multicode.use: The default height for every labelled control. An input and a select side by side must share it.

md.$description: Comfortable control height for primary actions in overlays.

com.multicode.use: Modal and drawer primary actions, where density relaxes.

compact.$description: Touch. Pointer 34px + 10, landing exactly ON the hit-target floor — the largest control IS the floor.

com.multicode.doNotUse: Inline chrome inside a modal — a row action or a section-header action in a settings tab is not the modal’s primary action, and takes sm or xs.

lg.$description: The app rail's glyph square: the one control drawn to be found from across the window rather than read in a row.

com.multicode.use: The app rail's section and tool glyphs, and the account + Settings cluster at its foot (owner ruling 2026-09-07: Slack's rail squares are a step above the product's largest control, and that step is what makes them findable). Pairs with icon.size.lg.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Anything inside a panel, a row, a toolbar or an overlay — those stop at md. This step exists for one column of window chrome, and a second consumer is a ruling, not a styling choice.

compact.$description: Touch. Pointer 40px + 10, keeping the ramp's constant lift.

hit-target-min.$description: The smallest permitted pointer target. A floor, not a size: every step of size.control.* clears it.

com.multicode.use: Minimum interactive area. A control drawn smaller than this pads out to it with a transparent hit area.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Shrinking a target below this because the glyph inside is small.

compact.$description: Touch. 44pt is the iOS HIG minimum and Material's 48dp rounds to the same intent; the pointer scale's 24px is a mouse target and would be unpressable with a thumb.

platforms.$note: See sem.font.size.body's platforms note for what `compact` is and why it is annotation rather than a third CSS mode. In short: the touch scale, same names, different values, not consumed by build-tokens.mjs.

com.multicode.use: The one focus-ring thickness, everywhere.

ring-offset.$description: The transparent gap between a focused control and its focus outline.

com.multicode.use: outline-offset, wherever focus.ring is applied. The gap is what keeps focus readable on a control whose own fill is the accent: color.border-focus and accent.primary resolve to the same hue, so a zero-offset ring on an accent fill has nothing to contrast against.
com.multicode.doNotUse: A wider offset to make focus louder — the gap is spatial separation, not emphasis.

ring.$description: The single focus treatment: an outline drawn on :focus-visible at focus.ring-offset.

com.multicode.use: Keyboard focus on every interactive element. Apply as `outline` on :focus-visible together with focus.ring-offset, never on :focus. An outline rather than a box-shadow ring: the offset gap is transparent and shows whatever surface is actually behind the control, where a ring offset has to be told that background and gets it wrong the moment the control changes surface.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Hover, selection, or validation — focus is its own signal and never shares a treatment. Never at a zero offset, and never suppressed without a replacement.

blur.$description: Backdrop blur radius of the one glass surface — the toast card.

com.multicode.use: The toast card only (owner ruling 2026-09-04): a corner-sized surface whose blur area is a fraction of the viewport. Dark mode blurs a little more because the lighter glass over near-black needs it to read as a pane.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Any scrim, modal, drawer, popover, menu, or full-width surface — blur over terminal panes re-samples every frame and was measured at ~10fps on a full-window scrim. The conformance lint pins glass to the toast.

opacity.$description: How much of bg.surface-raised the glass keeps; the rest is the page showing through.

com.multicode.use: The toast card's ground: color-mix(bg.surface-raised, glass.opacity) over the blur. Where backdrop-filter is unsupported the card falls back to solid bg.surface-raised.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Tinting any other surface translucent.

saturation.$description: Saturation boost applied with the blur so what shows through stays lively rather than grey.

com.multicode.use: Paired with glass.blur in the toast's backdrop-filter. Dark mode boosts less: near-black grounds have little to saturate and over-boosting shows as colour fringing.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Anywhere glass.blur is not.

com.multicode.use: The stacking order of overlay surfaces. Pick the layer by what the surface is, never by trial and error.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Arbitrary z-index values. A surface that needs to sit between two layers is a sign the surface is the wrong kind.

sticky.$description: Sticky panel headers and column headers.

com.multicode.use: The stacking order of overlay surfaces. Pick the layer by what the surface is, never by trial and error.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Arbitrary z-index values. A surface that needs to sit between two layers is a sign the surface is the wrong kind.

pane.$description: In-flow depth: docked panes and in-canvas floating chrome (a side pane, a canvas toolbar, an agent bubble) — above sticky headers, below every overlay.

com.multicode.use: The in-flow depth step for chrome that floats within a pane or canvas without leaving the document flow: docked side panes, canvas toolbars and rails, in-canvas bubbles. Sits above `z.sticky` so a docked pane covers the headers behind it; sits below `z.drawer`, so every overlay still wins.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Anything that scrims, traps focus or portals to the body — that is an overlay and takes `z.drawer`, `z.modal`, `z.popover`, `z.menu` or `z.toast`. Never a raw `z-20` utility: consume the token so the ladder stays one ladder.

float.$description: In-flow depth: panel-internal popovers and HUDs that float over a pane's own content — above docked panes, below every overlay.

com.multicode.use: The top in-flow depth step: a panel-internal popover, HUD or tray that floats over its own pane's content and must clear a docked `z.pane` sibling, but stays inside the pane and portals nowhere. Sits directly below `z.drawer`.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Surfaces that leave their pane (portalled popovers, menus, dialogs) — they take the overlay layers. Never a raw `z-30` utility, and never a value between this and `z.drawer`: a surface that needs one is the wrong kind of surface.

com.multicode.use: The stacking order of overlay surfaces. Pick the layer by what the surface is, never by trial and error.
com.multicode.doNotUse: Arbitrary z-index values. A surface that needs to sit between two layers is a sign the surface is the wrong kind.

popover.$description: Popover, Select listbox, and Tooltip. Above modal, so a dialog-hosted picker paints over its host's scrim.
